paper.title: Role of Metformin on Osteoblast Differentiation in Type 2 Diabetes.

evidence.snippet: Both metformin and rotenone, an inhibitor of respiratory chain complex I, suppressed glucose-6-phosphatase (G6pc), a rate limiting enzyme of liver glucose production, mRNA expression in a rat hepatoma cell line accompanied by a reduction of intracellular ATP concentration and an activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK).
evidence.explanation: Metformin behaves like an inhibitor of respiratory chain complex I.

paper.title: Metformin suppresses glucose-6-phosphatase expression by a complex I inhibition and AMPK activation-independent mechanism.

evidence.snippet: These changes activate the cellular energy sensor AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Thus, the increased cellular AMP/ATP ratio causes a dramatic and progressive activation
evidence.explanation: Inhibition of complex I raises the AMP/ATP ratio, which activates AMPK.

paper.title: Role of Metformin on Osteoblast Differentiation in Type 2 Diabetes.

evidence.snippet: These drugs, such as metformin and STZ, inhibit ATP synthesis in mitochondria to raise AMP/ATP ratio in the process of AMPK activation.
evidence.explanation: Complex I inhibition by metformin raises AMP/ATP ratio and activates AMPK.

paper.title: Mitochondrial inhibitor as a new class of insulin sensitizer.

evidence.snippet: TORC2 is a critical target of LKB1/AMPK signals in the regulation of gluconeogenesis. Finally, we show that metformin, one of the most widely prescribed type 2 diabetes therapeutics, requires LKB1 in the liver to lower blood glucose levels.
evidence.explanation: AMPK (activated via LKB1) negatively regulates gluconeogenesis via TORC2 suppression.

paper.title: The kinase LKB1 mediates glucose homeostasis in liver and therapeutic effects of metformin.

evidence.snippet: Metformin, which is widely prescribed for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients, regulates blood sugar by inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis and promoting insulin sensitivity to facilitate glucose uptake by cells.
evidence.explanation: AMPK activation by metformin is responsible for inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis.

paper.title: New Insight into the Effects of Metformin on Diabetic Retinopathy, Aging and Cancer: Nonapoptotic Cell Death, Immunosuppression, and Effects beyond the AMPK Pathway.

evidence.snippet: Metformin lowers blood glucose levels by inhibiting hepatic glucose production (HGP), an effect originally postulated to be due to a hepatic AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Inhibition of gluconeogenesis (hepatic glucose production) by the AMPK pathway lowers blood glucose, treating type 2 diabetes.

paper.title: Metformin activates a duodenal Ampk-dependent pathway to lower hepatic glucose production in rats.

evidence.explanation: Biguanides like metformin treat type 2 diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, establishing the link between gluconeogenesis inhibition and disease treatment.

paper.title: Oral antidiabetic agents: current role in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
